construct: MEN2 is caused by heterozygous germline gain-of-function variants in RET, which encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase. Constitutive or dysregulated RET signaling promotes C-cell and adrenal medullary tumorigenesis; MEN2A also predisposes to parathyroid hyperplasia/adenoma.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Familial medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and hyperparathyroidism with a heterozygous RET variant identifies MEN2A; RET is a proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase activated by germline gain-of-function variants.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: MEN1, NF1, VHL, and SDH syndromes are plausible endocrine/neoplastic alternatives, but the exact MEN2A triad plus pathogenic RET variant uniquely supports receptor-tyrosine-kinase gain of function.
